html:
The Pantheon is a Roman temple to all the gods in Rome, rebuilt in its present form under the emperor Hadrian between about 113 and 125. The first temple on the site was built by Agrippa in the reign of Augustus, and burned down. Hadrian kept Agrippa's name in the inscription on the front.

Behind a columned porch sits a round hall under a dome 43 m across. The height to the top of the dome is the same as its width, so a perfect sphere would fit inside. A round opening at the top, the oculus, is the only light source. The dome is made of Roman concrete, with lighter stone mixed in higher up, and it is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

In 609 the emperor Phocas gave the building to the pope, and it became the church of Saint Mary and the Martyrs. That use saved it, and it is one of the best preserved buildings of ancient Rome. Its dome inspired builders from Michelangelo to the architects of many modern capitols and libraries.
